reviews.review:
There is a lot that I like about this game, and I will probably play it once ever few months just to watch things explode... but that is for sure the highlight of the game.  It truly looks beautiful and can be mesmerizing.  However, every time I end up playing it, I am always end up saying things like, "what the f--- just  hit me?" or "how did I just freaking die?"  Basically, after the first level, the visual clarity goes out the window.  The outline of most enemies become practically invisible and you can only clearly see the middle of them, which is a huge problem when there are like 300 enemies spawning all over the place constantly.  For that reason alone, unfortunately, it gets put in the not recommended category.  

I also want to add that as far as I can tell, this is not a rhythm game although it is labeled as one.  The music is really cool and there is a thumping on the controller's vibration generators, but you never have to stay on beat to do anything.  But there is something about the controls that I like, and that is the ability to control where you are shooting if you want to.  If you don't aim, it will automatically aim for you, but I like being able to choose to aim if I want to.  

Basically, this game does some things pretty well, but the incredible lack of visual clarity completely ruins it for me and makes me not want to play it for more than a couple runs at a time.  I beat it once, and it was by using a character with a dash that kinda cheeses the game.  If you are looking for some cheap vector-exploding thrills, you might like this one a lot though.
